title: Test the feature, then pick a code path
purpose: See how a feature test picks the enhanced or the fallback code path in each browser.
sequence_reason: The test runs first and its yes or no answer decides which code runs next, so the learner must see the cause before the effect.
summary: A page tests a feature before it uses it. The @supports rule tests CSS in CSS, CSS.supports runs the same test in JavaScript, and the in operator checks that an object such as navigator has a member such as geolocation. A true answer runs the enhanced code, a false answer runs the fallback code. Some features cannot be tested, so pages load polyfills, and the polyfill.io takeover in 2024 shows that third-party polyfill code runs with your page. Origin trials turn an experimental feature on with a token until the trial expires, so the fallback must stay.
explanation: Feature detection asks the browser what it can do at run time and branches on the answer, so every visitor gets a working page.

learning_check.question: A browser has no Geolocation API. What does the code if ("geolocation" in navigator) { … } else { … } run?
learning_check.answer: The else branch, which offers static maps, because the in test returns false.

scenes.heading: Test the feature, not the browser
scenes.narration: Your code asks one question: can this browser do it? The answer picks the enhanced code or the fallback code.

scenes.heading: Three ways to ask
scenes.narration: The screen shows three feature tests. The @supports rule tests CSS inside CSS. CSS.supports runs the same test in JavaScript. The in operator checks an object member.

items: CSS.supports(): the CSS test in JavaScript
"geolocation" in navigator: a JS member check

scenes.heading: One test, two layouts
scenes.narration: CSS.supports asks the browser about grid-template-columns subgrid. True: the page links subgrid-layout.css. False: the link does not change, and the default layout stays.

scenes.heading: Check that the member exists
scenes.narration: The in operator asks if navigator has a geolocation member. If yes, the page uses the Geolocation API. If no, the else branch offers static maps.

terms.note: the browser object that holds it
runs when it is missing: static maps

scenes.heading: Polyfills run on your page
scenes.narration: Some features cannot be tested, so you may load a polyfill. Its code runs on your page. In 2024, the polyfill.io domain was sold, and its script was changed to inject malware into more than 100,000 sites.

scenes.heading: Experimental features expire
scenes.narration: An origin trial lets your site use an experimental feature. You register, get a token, and add the token to your page. When the trial expires, the feature is gone, so keep the fallback.

scenes.heading: Detect, then branch
scenes.narration: Test the feature, run the enhanced path when it exists, and keep a working fallback when it does not.
